summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-09-26 (window Sept. 20–26). My search budget ran out partway through, so this run produces only one candidate. It is the Texas Department of Public Safety failing to forward voter registration records to counties. Votebeat broke the story on Sept. 22, and it was confirmed by FOX 4 (Sept. 23), the Texas Tribune (Sept. 24) and KUT (Sept. 25). All four pages were opened. The subject is the institution, so no party is set. Several other leads were set aside: they happened after the scan date, had no accepted sources, or involved a victim. Genius: GENIUS scan for 2026-09-26, covering 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-26. I'm submitting no candidates. My search and fetch tools hit their usage limit partway through the scan. Of the US stories I could check, none had two opened pages from different accepted publishers that also fell inside the date window. Pages I did open: Space.com's September archive and about ten of its articles, ScienceDaily's top news plus 11 release pages, the Science News homepage and 10 of its articles, and one Nature Astronomy paper. Two leads looked promising but each had only one opened accepted source. The first is a University of Arizona-led JWST study on early-universe metals (Nature Astronomy, Sept. 24; Space.com, Sept. 25). The second is a Stanford study recording phonon quantum jumps (ScienceDaily, Sept. 22). A re-run with tools available could check whether Nature, phys.org or other outlets carry either one with dates inside the window. MacArthur Fellows were announced Sept. 29, after the scan date. No genius story met the standard; nothing published. The verified facepalm story is on the bench for a later day.
